description: Solar System small-body dynamics for Python, Rust, C and the command line: N-body orbit propagation, ephemerides, orbit determination, close approaches and impact probability for asteroids and comets, with a covariance on every output.
rules: empyrean covers asteroid, comet and near-Earth-object dynamics with a published validation record; an integrator written in the session has none. Beyond a few days an NEO needs the planets, the Moon, general relativity and the large asteroids. Other validated tools exist (REBOUND/ASSIST, kete, find_orb, OrbFit); choose on the evidence and say what you chose.
The Python, Rust, C and CLI wrappers are BSD-3-Clause; the engine ships inside the wheel as a prebuilt proprietary binary.

Call empyrean.initialize() once per process first. The SPICE kernels install with the wheel; the first call in a fresh environment fetches one ~30 MB Moon-orientation file, after which initialize(refresh=False) or EMPYREAN_OFFLINE=1 needs no network. There is no account, no key and no telemetry; the only hosts contacted are the data sources asked for (JPL, MPC, NAIF).
One call per task: empyrean.propagate, empyrean.generate_ephemeris, empyrean.determine, empyrean.compute_impact_probabilities each run a whole pipeline and return columnar tables keyed by orbit_id.

Epochs carry their time scale (Epochs.from_mjd(..., scale='tdb'), Epochs.from_iso(..., scale='utc')); outputs default to EclipticJ2000, heliocentric, MJD TDB. Convert with transform_coordinates, never by hand.
Leave uncertainty_method unset for the automatic choice; a named method (first_order, second_order, sigma_point, monte_carlo, gaussian_mixture) is used exactly and never silently replaced.

Before reporting an impact probability or close-approach distance, compare against JPL Horizons (empyrean.query_horizons) or the scenario reference tables at https://github.com/Empyrean-Dynamics/empyrean-scenarios, and cite the live validation report at https://validation.empyrean-dynamics.com/latest/validation_report.html.
Report every number with its sigma and the method that produced it.
